<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:avg_max_rate}
Consider an $(N,K,\mathbf{M},\mathbf{F})$ heterogeneous demand-private coded caching scheme satisfying \eqref{Eq_priv_cond_hetero}. The demand-privacy constraint in \eqref{Eq_priv_cond_hetero}. Then, we have
\begin{align}
    I\left(
    \overline D; X_{\overline D}
    \right)= &  I\left( D_k;X_{\overline D} 
    \right) +  I\left(
    \overline D_{-k};X_{\overline D}| D_k 
    \right) \notag\\
    = & I\left(
    \overline D_{-k};X_{\overline D}| D_k 
    \right) \label{eq:Tx_demn_1}\\
    = & 0. \label{eq:Tx_demn_2}
\end{align}
where \eqref{eq:Tx_demn_1}  follows from the demand privacy condition for user $i\neq k$ and \eqref{eq:Tx_demn_2} follows from the demand privacy condition for user $k$. Thus, $X_{\overline D}$ is independent of the
entire demand vector $\overline D$. In particular,
for any $\overline d_1,\overline d_2\in[N]^K$,
\begin{align}
&H(X_{\overline D}\mid
  \overline D=\overline d_1)
\nonumber =
H(X_{\overline D}\mid
  \overline D=\overline d_2).
\end{align}
 Consequently, without loss of generality (w.l.o.g.), it suffices to consider the worst-case transmission rate. In the remainder of the paper, we assume that the demand vector $\overline D$ is uniformly distributed over $[N]^K$ and denote $R_{\max}$ simply by $R$.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:drs}
    Consider a non-private coded caching system with $N$ files of sizes
    $\mathbf{F} = (F_0, F_1, \dots, F_{N-1})$ and $NK$ users partitioned
    into $K$ stacks of $N$ users each. Every user in the $k$-th stack
    ($k \in [K]$) has cache size $M_k$, giving the expanded cache size
    vector
    \begin{equation}
    \mathbf{M}_{\text{exp}} = \bigl(
            \underbrace{M_0,\dots,M_0}_{N},
            \underbrace{M_1,\dots,M_1}_{N}, \dots,
            \underbrace{M_{K-1},\dots,M_{K-1}}_{N}
        \bigr).
        \label{eq:m_exp}
    \end{equation}
    Let the demand vector $\overline{d}\in[N]^{NK}$ of the $NK$ users be
    partitioned according to the $K$ stacks as
\begin{align}
    \overline{d}
    =
    \bigl(
        \overline{d}^{(0)},
        \overline{d}^{(1)},
        \ldots,
        \overline{d}^{(K-1)}
    \bigr),
\end{align}
where $\overline{d}^{(k)}\in[N]^N$ denotes the demand vector of the $N$
users in the $k$-th stack. Define the \emph{restricted demand subset}
    $\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{RS}} \subset [N]^{NK}$ as
    \begin{align}
        \mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{RS}} = &\Bigl\{
            \overline{d} \in [N]^{NK} : \overline{d}^{(k)} \text{ is a cyclic shift of } \nonumber\\& \qquad (0, 1, \dots, N-1), \; \forall k \in [K]
        \Bigr\}.
        \label{eq:drs_set}
    \end{align}
    An $(N, NK, \mathbf{M}_{\text{exp}}, \mathbf{F}, R)$ non-private
    coded caching scheme that achieves rate $R$ for all demand vectors
    in $\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{RS}}$ is called an
    $(N, NK, \mathbf{M}_{\text{exp}}, \mathbf{F}, R)$
    $\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{RS}}$-non-private heterogeneous scheme.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:drs_reduction}
    If there exists an $(N, NK, \mathbf{M}_{\text{exp}}, \mathbf{F}, R)$
    $\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{RS}}$-non-private heterogeneous scheme, then there exists
    an $(N, K, \mathbf{M}, \mathbf{F}, R)$-private heterogeneous
    scheme.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{proof:thm_extnded}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:exact_tradeoff}
For $N=K=2$, an $(N,K,\mathbf M,\mathbf F, R) = (2,2,M_0,M_1, F_0, F_1, R)$  exists for $F_0 \geq F_1$ if and
    only if
    \begin{align}
        R &\ge F_0 + F_1 - 2M_0, \tag{DP1}\\[3pt]
        R &\ge F_0 + F_1 - 2M_1, \tag{DP2}\\[3pt]
        R &\ge (3F_0 + 2F_1 - 2M_0 - M_1)/3, \tag{DP3}\\[3pt]
        R &\ge (3F_0 + 2F_1 - M_0 - 2M_1)/3, \tag{DP4}\\[3pt]
        R &\ge F_0 + 0.5F_1 - M_0, \tag{DP5}\\[3pt]
        R &\ge F_0 + 0.5F_1 - M_1, \tag{DP6}\\[3pt]
        R &\ge 0.5(F_0 + F_1 - M_0), \tag{DP7}\\[3pt]
        R &\ge 0.5(F_0 + F_1 - M_1). \tag{DP8}
    \end{align}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
See Section~\ref{sec:proofs}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:thm_exact_N_K_2}
For $F_1\geq F_0$, the exact demand-private
memory-rate region is obtained by exchanging
$F_0$ and $F_1$ in
\Cref{thm:exact_tradeoff}.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
For $F_1\geq F_0$, relabel the files as
$W_0'=W_1$ and $W_1'=W_0$, and the demands
as $D_k'=1-D_k$ for $k\in[2]$.
This relabeling is a bijection on $[2]^2$
that preserves the uniform demand distribution,
decodability, and demand privacy, without
changing the cache capacities or transmission rate.
The result therefore follows from
\Cref{thm:exact_tradeoff}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- claim-1: body_md -->
\label{claim:region_partition}
The regions $\mathcal{R}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{R}_8$ defined in \eqref{eq:def_region}
form a partition of the cache-size domain
$[0,F_0+F_1]^2$.
Specifically,
\begin{align}
\bigcup_{i=1}^{8}\mathcal{R}_i
&=[0,F_0+F_1]^2,
\end{align}
and
\begin{align}
\operatorname{int}(\mathcal{R}_i)
\cap
\operatorname{int}(\mathcal{R}_j)
&=\emptyset,
\qquad \forall i\neq j.
\end{align}
<!-- end claim-1 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:partition_proof}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:converse}
    Let $\tilde{i} = (i+1) \bmod 2$ for $i=0,1$. Then any demand-private scheme for $N=K=2$ satisfies the following for $j=0,1$:
    \begin{align}
        (X, Z_1, W_{j} \mid D_1=j) &\sim (X, Z_1, W_{j} \mid D_0=i, D_1=j) \notag\\
        &\sim (X, Z_1, W_{j} \mid D_0 = \tilde{i}, D_1=j) \label{Eq_priv_cond3}
    \end{align}
    and
    \begin{align} 
        (X, Z_0, W_{j} \mid D_0=j) &\sim (X, Z_0, W_{j} \mid D_0=j, D_1=i) \notag\\
        &\sim (X, Z_0, W_{j} \mid D_0 = j, D_1=\tilde{i}). \label{Eq_priv_cond4}
    \end{align}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
